We used ROUGE to measure the quality of different summarization model outputs. We reported full-length F1 based ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-L scores on CNNDM, while we used the limited-length recall based ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-L on NYT.

We also evaluated abstractive systems by eliciting human judgements. 10 participants are presented with a document and a list of outputs generated by different abstractive summarization systems. Then they are asked to rank the outputs of these systems from best to worst according to informativeness (does the summary capture the informative part of the document?), fluency (is summary grammatical?), and succinctness (does the summary express the document clearly in a few words?).
